facts.raw_span: A 35-year-old woman presented with neck pain after a motor vehicle accident
15-year history of migraine headaches
migraine headaches had become more severe and positional (worse when lying down) over the past year
3 months of memory impairment and dizziness
1 year of gradual-onset tinnitus and dysphagia
Physical examination was unremarkable
Noncontrast CT of the head revealed a mass in the left cerebellomedullary cistern isodense to gray matter without calcifications
CT angiography showed displacement of the prepontine vessels without encasement
MRI demonstrated a 3.4×3.3×3.3 cm, well-circumscribed mass in the left cerebellomedullary and premedullary cisterns
mass was hyperintense to CSF on T1- and T2-weighted images
mass did not restrict diffusion
mass exerted mass effect on the brainstem and cerebellum without surrounding edema
